question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Major Trade Commodities — Regional Source Hubs]
options: Indigo — Produced mainly in Sarkhej (Gujarat) and Bayana (Rajasthan)
Saltpetre — Sourced primarily from Bihar (Eastern India) for gunpowder manufacture
Cotton Textiles — Exported from the Coromandel Coast (Southeastern India) and Gujarat (Western India)
Pepper & Cardamom — Sourced from the dry plains of Rajasthan (Northwestern India)
wrong_fact: Pepper and cardamom were spices sourced from the humid, tropical Malabar Coast of southwestern India (modern Kerala), NOT from the dry desert plains of Rajasthan.
explanation: Pepper, cardamom, and other high-value spices required tropical climatic conditions and were sourced predominantly from the Malabar Coast (southwestern India), especially ports like Cochin, Calicut, and Cannanore. Sarkhej in Gujarat and Bayana in Rajasthan were famous for high-quality indigo. Saltpetre, crucial as an ingredient for gunpowder, was extensively collected from Bihar. Cotton textiles were the mainstay of exports from Coromandel (Madras, Masulipatnam) and Gujarat (Surat).

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Export Commodities — Primary English Port/Hub]
options: Silk and Muslin — Kasimbazar and Dacca in Bengal
Calicoes (Cotton) — Madras and Masulipatnam on the Coromandel Coast
Saltpetre — Patna in Bihar shipped via Bengal ports
Saffron and Pepper — Ahmedabad and Surat in Gujarat
wrong_fact: Saffron is cultivated in Kashmir, and pepper is native to the Malabar Coast (southwestern India). Gujarat was famous for cotton textiles, indigo, and saltpetre, NOT for producing or exporting saffron and pepper.
explanation: Gujarat's primary trade commodities for the English were cotton cloth (baftas), indigo (from Sarkhej), and saltpetre. Saffron is grown in Kashmir (Northern India) and pepper is native to the Malabar Coast of southwestern India (Kerala). Silk and muslin were Bengal's specialties, calicoes were Coromandel's main export, and saltpetre was mined in Bihar and shipped down the Ganges to Bengal ports.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [English EIC Commodity Routes — Destination Markets]
options: Coromandel Cotton Textiles — Shipped to Bantam and Achin (Southeast Asia) to purchase spices
Bengal Saltpetre — Shipped to England for gunpowder manufacturing
Malwa Opium — Shipped to Europe as a luxury food preservative
Gujarati Indigo — Shipped to London for use in the British textile dyeing industry
wrong_fact: Opium was NOT shipped to Europe as a food preservative. It was shipped to China and Southeast Asia (and used as a narcotic/medicinal drug), whereas food preservatives in Europe were salt and spices (like pepper and cloves).
explanation: Opium, produced in Malwa and Bihar, was shipped to China and Southeast Asia (the 'carrying trade' or Eastern trade) in exchange for tea and silk, or as a highly profitable narcotic drug. It was never used as a food preservative in Europe (which relied on salt and spices like pepper). The Coromandel cotton textiles were highly valued in Southeast Asia (Bantam, Achin) and were exchanged by the English to buy spices. Saltpetre was sent to England to make gunpowder. Gujarati indigo went to England to dye woolens and cottons.
